key_insight: Composition anisotropy in 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics enables an unexpectedly large bulk photovoltaic field along the non-polar vertical direction—up to two orders of magnitude stronger than along the polar in-plane direction.
engineering_relevance: This points to a new design rule for voltage-readout photodetectors and solar-harvesting devices: tune layered composition and anisotropy, not just polarization direction, to maximize photovoltage.
method: Compared bulk photovoltaic fields along polar in-plane and non-polar vertical axes in 2D hybrid perovskite ferroelectrics.
Linked the response to a shift-current mechanism coupled with inorganic photocarrier generation and an insulating organic layer.
Derived formulas to describe intensity- and thickness-dependent photovoltage behavior.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports photovoltage/EBPE magnitudes up to orders of magnitude above benchmark photoferroelectrics and the highest yet reported for 2D hybrid perovskites, with strong directional anisotropy.
watch_item: Performance depends on a delicate inorganic/organic compositional balance, so device reproducibility and stability may be sensitive to layer quality and structural anisotropy.
paper_title: Composition Anisotropy Drives Large Bulk Photovoltaic Fields Along the Non-polar Vertical Direction in 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectrics
